summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and coronary artery disease, was admitted with hematemesis, melena, and epigastric pain. Initial evaluation ruled out acute coronary syndrome. Laboratory results showed stable but low hemoglobin. An upper endoscopy revealed grade 1 esophageal varices and gastritis, with no active bleeding. A non-displaced fracture of the right thumb was also identified after a recent fall. The patient left against medical advice before formal discharge instructions could be provided, though he was informed of the need to abstain from alcohol, continue home medications, and follow up with primary care and hepatology. His condition at departure was stable.
problems: Alcoholic gastritis, without mention of hemorrhage
Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Closed fracture of middle or proximal phalanx or phalanges of hand
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
